rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance – Criminal History Screening Restrictions
rules.effectiveDateQuote: On April 14, 2020, Berkeley City Council passed the Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance (BMC 13.106).
rules.requirement: Housing providers cannot inquire about, use, or consider criminal history in rental advertising, applications, tenant selection, or decision-making. Providers cannot refuse to rent, terminate tenancy, demand higher deposits or rent, or refuse to add family members based on criminal history. They cannot disqualify tenants from rental assistance based on criminal history (with limited exceptions). If taking any action based on criminal history, the provider must give written notice and opportunity to respond.
rules.quotedSpan: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.
rules.coverageDescription: All residential rental housing in Berkeley, except owner-occupied properties with 1–3 units where an owner of record resides as their primary residence, and except units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back in accordance with BMC 13.76.130 A.9, and except units occupied by existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates. Lifetime sex offenders and Section 8 housing have limited exemptions.
exemptions: Owner-occupied properties (1–3 units) where an owner of record resides as primary residence
Units under rental agreement allowing owner to move back (BMC 13.76.130 A.9)
Units occupied by existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates
warnings: The text states 'lifetime sex offenders' and 'public housing/Section 8 properties limited exemptions' but does not fully specify the scope of these exemptions; the ordinance itself should be reviewed for details.

The ordinance allows owner-occupied properties and specific situations to be exempt, but the exact coverage calculation may depend on interpretation of 'primary residence' and other conditions in the full text.
